steps.description: This walkthrough looks only at the `Solidity interfaces`. Everything you see here represents the **public API** that an external caller (`EOA` or `contract`) can invoke.

Collateral flow – entry.  deposit() transfers yield tokens from the caller into the protocol, credits the chosen position ( recipientId==0 mints a fresh NFT) and returns the debt-denominated value of what was deposited.

Collateral flow – exit.  withdraw() burns freeCollateral from the position and sends the requested yield tokens to the supplied recipient, provided the action keeps the position above the LTV guard-rail.
Debt flow – issuance.  mint() draws newly-created debt tokens (alTokens) against the position’s collateral and transfers them to the recipient.
Debt flow – burning via alTokens.  burn() destroys a user-supplied amount of alTokens and credits the specified position, reducing its debt balance.

Debt flow – repaying with collateral tokens.  repay() lets the caller hand in yield tokens instead of alTokens; the tokens are forwarded to the Transmuter and an equivalent debt amount is cancelled on the target position.
Safety valve.  liquidate() can be called by anyone; if a position’s collateral ratio is below the required threshold it is partially or fully closed, seizing collateral and rewarding the liquidator.
Monitoring ‑ system wide.  `totalDebt()` (line 601) exposes the sum of all outstanding debt tokens, while `totalSyntheticsIssued()` (line 603) shows how many have actually been minted.

Monitoring ‑ position level.  `getCDP()`, `totalValue()` and `getMaxBorrowable()` allow front-ends to display collateral, debt and remaining borrowing power.  `freeCollateral` is not its own view but is maintained internally (see `Account` struct line 44) and is used when `getMaxBorrowable()` is computed.
**Admin controls** – selecting price sources.  `setTokenAdapter()` lets the admin replace the `oracle/adapter` that prices the yield token.
**Admin controls – revenue routing.**  `setTransmuter()` updates the address that receives yield-token flows (redemptions, repayments, liquidations).
Admin controls – fee vault.  `setAlchemistFeeVault()` points the protocol to a `FeeVault` that holds underlying tokens for liquidator bonuses.
**Initialization.**  The `initialize()` function wires up every immutable parameter – tokens, caps, collateralisation parameters, adapters and fee recipients – establishing a clean genesis state.
Position NFT API. Only the `AlchemistV3` contract is expected to call `mint()` and `burn()`; end-users touch these indirectly when opening or fully closing positions.

After this tour you now have the definitive list of callable functions:
- collateral lifecycle: `deposit()`, `withdraw()`
- debt lifecycle: `mint()`/`mintFrom()`, `burn()`, `repay()`
- safety: `liquidate()`/`batchLiquidate()`
- read-only monitors: `totalDebt()`, `totalSyntheticsIssued()`, `getCDP()`, `totalValue()`, `getMaxBorrowable()`, etc.
- admin knobs: `setTransmuter()`, `setTokenAdapter()`, `setAlchemistFeeVault()`, plus other ratio & pause setters.
- position NFT hooks: `mint()`, `burn()` – callable only by `AlchemistV3`.
